The 68-result formal core passed a replay using pinned sources, declaration-kind resolution, a transi-
tive axiom audit, and compiler controls. All 119 Lean source files and their mathematical hypotheses
remained unchanged. The 151-row reviewed map covers the full scoped statements of the 68 theorem-
like manuscript records. This verification checks the exact inherited statement contract. It does not
supply a new line-by-line mathematical proof of that correspondence.

The replay compiled all 118 production modules into an initially empty directory for project objects.
Each module ran separately with one Lean worker. The cumulative receipt fingerprints every successful
source and output object. The aggregate imports the completed production closure. The original audit
source and a generated declaration-kind consumer were then executed.

The compiler’s binary hash and commit were checked, and all nine external package Git revisions
matched the dependency manifest. Cached external objects were reused. The record therefore does not
claim a cold rebuild of Mathlib or an independently implemented proof kernel.

Production compilation
118 of 118 modules, with new project objects
Source preservation
All 119 Lean source files unchanged
Reviewed targets
1,164 targets: 953 theorems and 211 constructions
Namespace audit
2,234 declarations, including 1,999 theorem declarations
Compiler controls
Six accepted outcomes under explicit diagnostics
Verifier tests
42 verification tests and 10 integrity tests

Supporting and generated declarations contribute to these totals. The totals are not counts of inde-
pendent discoveries.

The exact runtime is Lean 4.34.0-rc2, commit 6a10ac8c22beadecabdbb0919c2b50214762f91d, with
Mathlib revision aeb72f1e9981b6d35b426b16dca7759be3e7ba06. The compiler’s SHA-256 fingerprint
is e8baaa71855a616dc351028f3ad2200051b0671f423a1696a100e809302d5550. The permitted transitive
axioms are propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

A valid projector-idempotence application is accepted. An explicit false theorem, an admitted proof,
an omitted premise, an injected custom axiom, and a definition presented as a theorem must produce
their intended rejection diagnostics. A timeout, signal kill, missing import, or unrelated API error does
not count as successful rejection.

The warning policy is material to this contract. The inherited -E warning setting accepted an isolated
deliberately admitted proof with exit code 0. The verified replay instead uses -DwarningAsError=true,
which rejected that fixture with exit code 1. The production mathematical sources were not weakened
or edited.
